intelligence.human_view: He saw it twice and named both halves of the failure in one breath: "not aligned with our buttons" (the design half) and "they don't make sense" (the function half). The eye then showed the failure was bigger than he saw — seven pills, not two, every one claiming the same "4 online", a count that cannot be real, on controls that open group chats while dressed as mail filters, with "All topics" unable to restore the mail at all. A count that is identical everywhere is decoration pretending to be information; a pill that opens a chat is a chat control, not a filter. Both halves have to hold: aligned with the standard, and doing what it says.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine seven buttons that all say "4 friends are here!" — but the number is the same on every one, and when you press one it doesn't do what you thought. That's not a helpful button! From now on, a button must say the true thing, and do the thing it says.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, those buttons at the top all say the same thing — "four online" — seven times over, and they don't do what they look like they do. A button should tell the truth and work the way it promises. We're fixing them so they match our buttons and make sense.
intelligence.naya_view: THE "FOUR ONLINE" BUTTONS ARE NO GOOD. NOT ALIGNED WITH OUR BUTTONS AND THEY DON'T MAKE SENSE. A COUNT THAT IS IDENTICAL EVERYWHERE IS NOT A COUNT — FIX THE COUNT OR REMOVE THE CLAIM. A PILL THAT OPENS A CHAT IS A CHAT CONTROL, NOT A MAIL FILTER. EVERY BUTTON ALIGNS WITH THE SYSTEM'S BUTTON STANDARD OR IT DOES NOT SHIP.
